transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-29
Time: 09:30 AM UTC
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Patel (Redwood SE), Arjun Rao (Redwood SE), Sara Morales (Nimbus Head of ML), David Kim (Nimbus Platform), Priya Rao (Nimbus Compliance), Ethan Zhou (Nimbus SRE)

Summary (auto):
Quick sync to review latest pilot results, agree on pinning priorities for model variants, and validate rollback and cutover criteria for the next pilot phase. Focus on latency, KV cache behaviour, and emergency fallbacks.

Topics:
- p50/p95/p99 latency comparisons across three variants (base, q8, q4_0)
- KV cache hit rates and prefix caching impact
- Pinning policy: soft pin vs hard pin and tie-breakers
- Rollback/escape hatch playbooks and routing priorities
- Compliance questions around audit logs and retention

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining on a friday, appreciate it. quick check, did i get the timezone right 09:30 UTC?
[00:08] Sara: yeah that's right for us. thanks maya.
[00:11] Maya: cool. quick agenda, we'll run through last week's bench numbers, liam's got a tuning suggestion, then we align on which variant to pin for the canary and what counts as an emergency rollback.
[00:23] Liam: yeah i'm gonna share my screen in a sec, but top line: q8 variant gives ~1.6x cost saving but p95 moves up about 70 ms for our 512 token median. q4_0 is cheaper but shows occasional 300-400ms spikes at p99 when the KV cache miss pattern happens.
[00:41] Sara: can you repeat that about the KV thing, we saw a couple of those in the customer-facing test yesterday. is it miss due to prefix length?
[00:49] Liam: sort of, it's a mixture. our instrumentation shows that when the prefix window exceeds 128 tokens and the incoming distribution has variable contexts, the a different code path for K V cache gets cold and we see additional fetches. that hits the p99 most.
[01:07] David: sorry to interrupt — by "different code path" do you mean the runtime switches kernels or it's an LRU eviction problem?
[01:13] Liam: good q. it's both — kernel selection slightly changes memory access patterns when quantized and the LRU-ish cache (red-wood's prefix cache) ends up thrashing when request sequences aren't well grouped. in practice we saw a KV hit rate drop from 92% to 64% on that test.
[01:31] Priya: that 64% - is that for hosted or private? we need to note that for compliance and S L A expectations.
[01:38] Liam: that run was hosted with dedicated routing to the pilot pool. Private deployment with local on-prem network had similar drops in spike frequency but still saw misses when sequence length varied.
[01:50] Maya: ok, thanks. sara, you sent a quick failures list earlier — did the team triage root causes?
[01:56] Sara: yes. two buckets: one is hallucination rate slightly higher for q4_0 on clinical intent prompts, the other is timeouts in the UI when p99 goes beyond 1.2s. we attached traces.
[02:08] Arjun: on the hallucination bit we ran eval sets and the q8 model's accuracy delta was acceptable; q4_0 had a few safety regression cases around dosage phrasing. we flagged those in the eval sheet.
[02:21] David: so leaning toward pinning q8 for the canary but maybe keep q4_0 as a fallback for lower cost paths?
[02:28] Liam: that's one option. i want to propose a "soft pin" policy: route 80% traffic to base or q8 depending on latency target, shadow 20% to q4_0 for quality monitoring; automatic fallback rule if p95 exceeds threshold or if KV hit rate drops under 70%.
[02:45] Sara: i like the shadow idea. question — how do we detect KV drop quickly enough to trigger fallback without false positives?
[02:53] Liam: the runtime emits per-request KV hit boolean and we have a rolling 5-minute window alert. proposed trigger: sustained drop below 70% over a 5-minute window with concurrent p95 > 800ms. that reduces noise.
[03:10] Ethan: if we do auto-fallback, does that keep user context? last time we lost some prefix context and user saw weird completions.
[03:18] Liam: critical point — fallback preserves request affinity, but there's an unavoidable cold KV for the new variant. we can mitigate with a quick warm-up step: pre-warm common prefixes or rehydrate the KV cache for active sessions in the transition window. that reduces user-visible glitches.
[03:36] Maya: ok, so we have two levers: pre-warm + thresholded auto-fallback. priya, anything on audit trail if we do automatic fallbacks?
[03:44] Priya: we need an immutable audit log entry for every automated switch — who/what triggered it, model versions, routing policy id, and timestamps. retention policy for pilot is 90 days but compliance might want 180 for certain records. we'll confirm.
[03:57] Sara: concerning pin types — what's the difference between "hard pin" and "soft pin" operationally?
[04:03] Liam: hard pin means traffic is forced to variant X for the selected route; no automated routing away. soft pin is a default preference that allows canary and structured fallbacks. hard pin is good for debugging or compliance locked windows; soft pin is safer for phased rollouts.
[04:20] David: we prefer soft pin for the first production-facing cut, and reserve hard pin for emergency rollback drills.
[04:27] Maya: noted. let's talk rollback playbook. liam, can you summarize your doc?
[04:33] Liam: sure. playbook steps: 1) detect (via p95/p99 SLA or KV hit rule), 2) alert and snapshot traces, 3) trigger soft-fallback to pre-approved fallback variant, 4) if fallback fails, execute hard-cut to last known good model and run routing circuit-breaker for 15 minutes, 5) notify ops + open incident in their tracker. I included CLI examples using the Redwood API: POST /v1/runtime/rollout with variant=golden and flag emergency=true. note: sometimes the API path differs for private control planes, we included curl + k8s job variants.
[05:15] Sara: will that preserve user tokens and avoid double-charges? finance is worried about cost double-write during transition.
[05:22] Arjun: the runtime supports request-level dedupe via idempotency keys; cost duplication only happens when retries occur. we recommend client-side idempotency and a short circuit in the sdk during the switch.
[05:33] David: about testing - we want a tabletop drill where we simulate KV miss and then force the fallback. timeline?
[05:38] Maya: propose next week tuesday 2027-01-03 for internal tabletop with SRE + ML. actual canary cutover week of 2027-01-12.
[05:48] Priya: compliance will need to be in the tabletop for the audit trail. also, retention change request for pilot logs — we'll need a written attestation.
[05:57] Maya: liam you mentioned a tuning suggestion earlier?
[06:01] Liam: yes — we can reduce p99 spikes by increasing batching window for short bursts (100-150ms) and by enabling relaxed kernel selection for quant variants which slightly increases throughput but evens out memory access. that reduces variance but may add tail latency for individual tokens. tradeoff is predictable.
[06:20] Sara: can we see a simulated run with the relaxed kernel setting? even synthetic is fine to convince product.
[06:26] Liam: i'll run it against the clinical prompt set and include golden samples in the spreadsheet.
[06:31] Maya: great. any competitors concerns?
[06:34] Sara: internal note — we evaluated Anthropic endpoints — latency was similar but cost was higher for our median throughput. openAI had better p99 in some microbenchmarks but lacked our prefix/K V cache controls. basically we're back to balancing cost vs control.
[06:52] Ethan: ops question — for private pilot, what's the minimum RBAC we need?
[06:56] Liam: we require a service account with create/list on the runtime resources and a role for audit logs push. we'll send a sample terraform snippet.
[07:05] David: on the sample terraform — can you make the V P C peering example explicit? last time we had network egress rules missing.
[07:11] Maya: will do.
[07:13] Sara: quick recap please — what are we pinning for the canary?
[07:17] Maya: decision: soft-pin q8 as primary for canary, shadow q4_0 at 20% for quality checks, base (float) reserved as emergency golden. triggers: auto-fallback if p95 > 800ms AND KV hit rate < 70% sustained 5 minutes. fallback action: soft-fallback to base then if problems persist executed hard-cut to golden.
[07:37] Priya: confirm audit retention ask — compliance recommends 180 days for automated switch logs. we'll file formal request.
[07:44] Maya: ok, action items recapped in the chat. liam will create a rollback playbook doc, and i'll send the trimmed latency csv by tomorrow. david will confirm networking roles.
[07:56] Sara: thanks everyone. we'll run internal tabletop and follow up with failures list by 2027-01-05.
[08:03] Maya: cool, i'll schedule the canary window in the shared calendar and invite ops + compliance. thanks all, enjoy your friday.

End of transcript.
